messages:
elena: FYI ran into an onboarding snag with the go generator sample. Canceling the parent ctx returns from Generate(), but the process keeps running because a background auth refresher is holding a blocking HTTP call. pprof shows goroutine stuck in the refresh path.

raf: ugh, that surprises new users. what's the sample doing?

elena: simplified flow: main starts a refresher goroutine (legacy TokenSource style) and then calls client.Generate(ctx, req). We cancel ctx on SIGTERM. Generate returns, cancel runs, but refresher keeps the process alive because it uses blockingFetchToken() with retries/backoff that don't observe ctx.

theo: two separate DX issues: (1) generator ergonomics — callers expect an explicit Cancel/Close that tears down internal io/backpressure; (2) auth code must be cancellable. New users assume a single ctx covers everything.

elena: right. I sketched two approaches in the ticket: offer Stream.Next(ctx) + Stream.Close() so callers can pass per-iteration cancellation, or keep convenience Generate(ctx, req) but guarantee it creates a child context that controls internal goroutines and is canceled on return.

raf: Next(ctx) is nice for explicit control and per-token timeouts, non-breaking can be: add new Stream API and keep Generate for convenience. For auth: provide NewContextAdapter(ts TokenSource) that runs refresh requests with supplied ctx so legacy token sources are cancellable.

theo: sample app short-term fixes: switch to signal.NotifyContext, and wrap legacy refresher with a context-aware helper. Also add a README FAQ: "Process doesn't exit after ctx cancel? Check cancellable token refresh + stream Close."

elena: here's a tiny example wrapper I used in the sample: 
```go
// adapter wraps old TokenSource and runs refresh with ctx-aware HTTP calls
func NewCtxTokenSource(ctx context.Context, ts TokenSource) TokenSource {
  return &ctxAdapter{ctx: ctx, base: ts}
}

// in sample main:
ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt)
defer stop()
// spawn refresher with ctx so blocking calls can be canceled
go func() { adapt := NewCtxTokenSource(ctx, legacyTS); runRefreshLoop(ctx, adapt) }()
_ = client.Generate(ctx, req)
```

raf: also add a unit/integration test pattern: start a net.Listener that accepts the token request but intentionally stalls (accept connection, sleep) to mimic a hung token endpoint. After cancel, assert process exits within N seconds. CI will catch regressions.

theo: SDK-level change proposals:
- non-breaking: Stream V2 that supports Next(ctx) and Close(); add NewContextTokenSource adapter.
- breaking but cleaner: make Generate return Stream and deprecate the old helper.

elena: agree. for immediate impact I'll open a sampleapp PR demonstrating the adapter + signal.NotifyContext + small test that simulates a stalled token server, and add a short blurb in generator onboarding checklist.

ci-bot: Created ticket RW-9023: "go sdk: generator stream ergonomics (Next(ctx)/Close) + context-aware token refresh adapter" and kicked off a job.

raf: great — please include a small test that simulates backoff sleeps too (use context-aware time.After or a cancellable backoff helper) so folks don't copy the naive time.Sleep patterns.

elena: will do. I'll link the PR in the ticket when ready. thanks for the reviews!
